Seawall vote

After months of debate the town council approved a plan on Thursday night to replace the crumbling seawall that lines the old harbor district. Supporters said the repairs could not wait another season, while opponents argued that the price had grown too large for a town of its size.

The measure passed five to four. Work is expected to begin in the spring, with the most exposed stretch near the ferry landing rebuilt first. Residents cheered when the final tally was read aloud in the crowded meeting room.

Engineers told the council that sections of the wall date to the 1930s and have shifted as much as eight inches since the last survey, leaving gaps that let water pour into low streets during high tides and storms.

The approved plan replaces the wall in three phases, starting with the ferry landing and ending at the public boat ramp. Each phase is designed to close no more than one block of the waterfront at a time so restaurants and shops can stay open.
